description: Fix language persistence bug - the settings service always returns hardcoded language 'ar' instead of reading/writing from the database. Add a settings table to store key-value pairs including language, and ensure the UI applies the language immediately and on reload.
steps: Step 1: Add a 'settings' table to src/db/schema.js with columns: id, key (TEXT UNIQUE), value (TEXT), updated_at. Add CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and an index on key.

Step 2: Update src/services/settings.js - rewrite getSettings() to read from the new settings table (falling back to defaults). Rewrite updateSettings() to upsert key-value pairs into the settings table. The language key must be stored and retrieved properly. Keep backward compatibility by also reading teacher_name/school_name/class_name from the profiles table if they exist there.

Step 3: Update src/renderer/js/screens/settings.js - after saveSettings(), apply the language change immediately by updating document.documentElement dir and lang attributes. Also update sidebar labels if language changes.

Step 4: Update src/renderer/js/app.js - on init(), call window.api.getSettings() and apply the stored language (set html dir='rtl'/'ltr', lang='ar'/'en'). This ensures language persists across navigation and restart.

Step 5: Add tests in tests/services/settings.test.js - test that getSettings returns defaults when no settings exist, that updateSettings persists language, that getSettings returns the persisted language value, and that updating other fields does not reset language.
acceptance_criteria: getSettings() returns the language that was last saved via updateSettings()
After calling updateSettings({language: 'en'}), subsequent getSettings() calls return language: 'en'
The settings table is created by schema.js
All existing tests continue to pass
verification: Run npx jest --no-coverage and confirm all tests pass including new settings tests
